newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunis bourse seeks soft landing after blast-off.
newsitem.headline: Tunis bourse seeks soft landing after blast-off.

text.p: After two years of explosive growth the Tunis share market has spent the last 12 months going nowhere.

But market officials say the market downturn is the price of a soft landing after rocketing growth and they hope that computerised dealing, due to start next week, will boost trading by improving transparency.
"Prices had exploded during the last two years. We must now secure a soft landing," Mohamed Hadouej, head of the Tunis Stock Exchange said.
"After a phase of euphoria, we are entering the age of reason," Finance Minister Nouri Zorgati told journalists when questioned about the market's drop in recent months.

At end-September the stock exchange index stood at 602.67, down six percent from 639.97 at end-September 1995. The index had risen 40 percent in the year to September 1995 and 99 percent in the previous 12 months.
The index closed at 599.78 on Tuesday.
Trading volume has also been falling despite an increase in the number of listed companies.

The value of shares traded dropped by 29 percent to 444 million dinars during the year to end-September, after rising 117 percent to 628 million in the year to September 1995 and 164 percent to 290 million in the previous year.

The value of turnover dropped much more on the primary market for fully-listed shares, by 64 percent between September 1995 and September 1996, to 186 million dinars ($190 million) compared to 520 million dinars previously.
Total market volume dropped by 25 percent to 18 million shares from 24 million shares the year before.

The number of listed companies reached 30 at the end of September, from 25 in the same month last year, and 20 in September 1994. As a result, capitalisation grew by 14 percent to 4.04 billion dinars at end-September from 3.55 billion a year before.

Brokers said investors chasing short-term gains had driven share prices above their real value. They said the market is not very liquid. Shares may have to drop further and the number of listings rise before the market recovers.
"The aim is to have 100 listed companies," Zorgati told brokers last month. ($=0.98 dinar)
